justification: Adds a plan, verifier and dry-run-only applier that would mark 5 served SEPP rows proven and re-copy 38 more from the law's own unit text. A row is planned only when the law unit relates to its ref_number, because proven makes the site show that clause number as checked. Nothing is written to production by this branch: the apply script is dry-run by default and was not run with --apply. Standard rather than critical because the only write path is gated behind a verifier that re-derives every row and an explicit flag, and all rows keep a backup and version history.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_sepp_marker_blind.py -o addopts= -q && python scripts/verify_sepp_marker_blind.py data/sepp_marker_blind_plan_2026-10-18.json data/sepp_marker_blind_evidence_2026-10-18.jsonl
falsifiable_check.fails_when: A rule is loosened or a proof is altered. Twenty-two single-line mutations were applied to the scripts and the tests re-run: marker removal off, the attached-marker guard off, size cap 3x raised to 300x, coverage floor 0.9 lowered to 0.3, the number check off, the ambiguity refusal off, the peer check off, the repeated-run refusal off, the ref_number preference off, the minimum word count off, the ref_related filter off in rule 1 and in rule 2, the span floor 0.9 set to 0, the excerpt flag removed, the full-unit preference removed, the excerpt refusal renamed, and five verifier checks off. Twenty were killed; the two survivors are verifier checks (offset slice and field diff) that are redundant with each other. The verifier on the real plan reports 45 verified, 0 mismatches.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The law snapshots in data/law_text_cache, pinned by sha256 in manifest.json, are the authority. The verifier re-parses the snapshot HTML and recomputes every verdict from the stored row text; it does not trust the plan's offsets, unit ids or new text.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: With SIZE_MAX raised from 3.0 to 300.0 the command printed 'FAILED tests/test_sepp_marker_blind.py::test_rule2_unit_more_than_3x_the_row_refused' and '1 failed, 24 passed'; restored, it printed 25 passed.

pre_impl.existing_data: scripts/state_law_recopy.py, state_law_proof.py, apply_state_law_recopy.py and apply_state_law_proof.py already exist on main and are reused for the unit parser, snapshot cache, number extraction, the verbatim-in-law check and the versioned writer. The classification CSV from the earlier worktree supplies only which rows are in scope; every verdict is recomputed from the database row and the snapshot.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I first assumed the existing 90 percent run-share unit picker could choose the unit. It cannot tell equal units apart and has no offsets, so a separate exact-sequence finder was written. Also, markers such as (a) cannot be stripped everywhere: 5(2) would lose its subclause, so a marker attached to a preceding letter or digit is kept.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Three new scripts and one test file. The applier imports check_plan and md5 from apply_state_law_recopy and the version writer from dq88_refresh_2026_10_10 rather than copying them.

functions.name: decide
functions.input: the stored row text, its ref_number and a parsed law snapshot
functions.output: a verdict dict: accept with unit and word offsets, recopy with coverage and new text hash, or refuse with a reason
functions.if_none: an empty or missing row text yields fewer than 8 words and is refused as too_short; a missing ref_number only removes the unit preference and leaves the unique-smallest rule

functions.name: norm_tokens
functions.input: any text, a stored row or a snapshot unit
functions.output: the list of letter and digit runs after list markers, dashes, bullets and punctuation are removed
functions.if_none: None becomes an empty string and an empty list, which downstream is refused as too_short

functions.name: verify
functions.input: the plan dict, the evidence rows and the cache directory
functions.output: a count of verified rows and a list of mismatch messages
functions.if_none: no evidence rows returns zero verified, which the command line turns into exit 2 so an empty check cannot pass

queries.sql: SELECT id, document_id, ref_number, provision_text, md5(provision_text), citation_status, is_current, source_council, (SELECT count(*) FROM provision_versions v WHERE v.provision_id = p.id) FROM regulatory_provisions p WHERE id = ANY(%s)
queries.filters: id list from the classified CSV, bucket near_copy or copy_with_gaps; is_current and source_council IS NULL re-checked in Python and again in the applier
queries.purpose: Re-read the in-scope rows at plan time so every verdict uses the row's current text, md5, proven state and version count.
queries.where_clause: id = ANY(ids from the classified CSV); is_current and source_council IS NULL checked in Python

break_it.scenario: A row is a truncated excerpt of a long unit, such as one sentence of a clause, and still matches as an exact contiguous run.
break_it.what_happens: Rule 1 would mark it proven although the stored row stops before the clause ends and may have dropped a condition.
break_it.how: Rule 1 now needs the row to be at least 90 percent of the unit's words. A shorter run is re-copied as the whole unit under rule 2 or refused as excerpt (8 rows). Tests cover the recopy and the refusal.

break_it.scenario: The row's text is verbatim in a unit that is not the clause its ref_number names, such as ref 3D.22(7) with text only in sec.3D.21-ssec.7.
break_it.what_happens: Marking it proven makes the site show 3D.22(7) as a checked clause number when it is not.
break_it.how: A row is accepted or recopied only when the unit is the ref_number's unit or its parent or child. Otherwise it is refused as ref_mismatch (177 rows) and the unit found is listed in the refused CSV for a later ref fix. ref_number is never rewritten. Tests cover accept and recopy refusals.

break_it.scenario: The same text appears in several sibling codes or schedules, so the row could be a copy of any of them.
break_it.what_happens: Picking one would attach the row to a possibly wrong clause with no error.
break_it.how: Two or more matching related units with no ref_number match and no unique smallest unit are refused as ambiguous_unit. Tests cover the refusal and the ref_number tie-break for both rules.

break_it.scenario: A re-copy swaps in a unit whose numbers differ from the row, such as a different metre limit.
break_it.what_happens: The served rule would silently carry a different figure.
break_it.how: Every number in the old text must be in the unit text or the row is refused as number_missing (16 rows). A test changes 1 metre to 7 metre and expects the refusal.

break_it.scenario: The law snapshot file is replaced or edited after the plan was made.
break_it.what_happens: Offsets would point into different text.
break_it.how: The verifier compares the snapshot sha256 with the evidence, the plan manifest and the cache manifest, and the applier runs the verifier first.

break_it.scenario: A row is edited in the database between plan time and apply time, so the row's current text, md5, proven state or version count differs from the plan.
break_it.what_happens: The write would overwrite or prove text that was never checked, across any of the planned rows.
break_it.how: The applier refuses unless every row md5 equals the plan, is not already proven and has no version history for recopy rows, re-checks under FOR UPDATE, and rolls back on any rowcount or end-state mismatch.

break_it.scenario: The plan's source URL, epi or law_date is edited while the evidence is left alone.
break_it.what_happens: The applier writes the plan source as citation_source_path, so a false clause link would be stored on a proven row.
break_it.how: The verifier requires source to equal the canonical law URL plus the verified unit id, and epi and law_date to equal the evidence. The applier also refuses if ref_number changed since the plan, and recounts version history under the row lock.
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_sepp_marker_blind.py -o addopts= -q -k "source_url or law_date"

break_it.scenario: A ref_number names a paragraph, such as 3.29(3)(e), but the row's text is only found in the wider subclause.
break_it.what_happens: Proving or recopying against the subclause would show the paragraph citation as checked against text that is not that paragraph, and a recopy would replace the paragraph's text with the whole subclause.
break_it.how: ref_full resolves the whole ref to a unit id; a verdict whose unit is neither that unit nor inside it is refused as ref_more_specific_than_unit, as is a ref whose extra level cannot be resolved. A title in brackets such as 3D.61 (Excavation) is treated as a label. Tests cover the refusal, the accepted paragraph case and the label case.

mutation_analysis: Twenty-two one-line mutations were run against the scripts with the test file in place, each restored afterwards. Twenty were killed outright. Two verifier checks survive individually because the offset slice check and the evidence field diff both catch a tampered offset; this redundancy is deliberate and stated. Earlier survivors (coverage floor, repeated run, md5-only change) got their own tests and were re-run until killed. The ambiguity refusal for rule 1 only fires when two related units are both filled by the row, which the sec.10 fixture covers. For the paragraph rule five more mutations were run (check off, ancestor-only, always-true, unparseable level ignored, label branch off); all were killed.
residual_risk: 177 of 341 in-scope rows are refused for ref_mismatch because their ref_number is a topic label or provision id rather than a clause, so most of the unproven set stays unproven until a deterministic ref fix. A marker letter that is really a unit symbol, such as (m) for metres, is stripped on both sides and could hide a dropped symbol. The classification CSV is a snapshot; rows are re-read from the database at plan time but the in-scope list is fixed. No production write has been made. A ref naming a paragraph more specific than the chosen unit is now refused (ref_more_specific_than_unit, 2 rows).
